analyst_view.overall: Early view: Spurs under Roberto De Zerbi lost 1-0 at Leeds after three straight wins and lost Mathys Tel to injury in that game, adding to a list that already includes Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Mykhaylo Mudryk, Savio and Lucas Bergvall. Fulham under Alvaro Arbeloa drew 1-1 with Newcastle and tend to get plenty of the ball without finishing well. Two mid-table sides with blunt attacks.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean lower: both sides have scored only 10 goals in 10 games, Spurs are missing a long list of attackers, and Fulham's finishing let them down against Newcastle. Rodrigo Muniz's goal there was his first league goal in seven months.

corners.text: The site has 11.3 corners. I lean slightly lower: Spurs' injured players include most of their wide options (Odobert, Mudryk, Simons, Savio), which cuts the dribbling that wins corners. Fulham were pushed into long balls by Newcastle's man-to-man marking, which does not create many corners either.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I agree: Pedro Porro and De Zerbi were both booked at Leeds, but De Zerbi's touchline ban is for the Ipswich game on 21 November and will be served by then. Nothing else points either way.

shots.text: The site has 27.3 shots. I lean lower: Spurs' creative absences and Fulham's tendency to keep the ball without breaking through both point to fewer shots. Mid-20s fits better.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. I lean lower: Spurs were called poor at Leeds and created little, and Fulham missed clear chances against Newcastle. Seven on target is more realistic.
